payload.author: impl:B@run-160
payload.body:
Task B approach (run-160): six edits in fleet/publish-fold.mjs, no exam file of my own (the peer writes fleet/tests/test_publish_fold.mjs at the guarded path).

1. M1: add `onEvent: eventLog.onEvent` to the `resolveConflicts({...})` call — resolveConflicts already spreads `resolverReceiptOf` onto a non-RESOLVED `resolver:reply` row at this base, so M1 is one option on one call.
2. M2: both `driver:publish-fold` append sites (the fresh one inside `record`, the replayed one in the completed-attempt branch) become `eventLog.onEvent(publishFoldEvent(row, conflictsIndex()))`; `record` loses its now-derived `pathsConflicted` parameter, and the replay site stops hard-coding `pathsConflicted: 0`.
3. M3: `writeResolverBriefs` gains `receipts = []` and appends `factsBlock(receipts, [conflict.path])`; `publishFold` reads `receiptRows(<runDir>/events.jsonl)` ONCE at attempt start (before anything this attempt appends) and hands it over.
4. M3: one `driver:facts` {label: 'resolve:publish-fold:<attemptKey>:<i>', receipts: <ids>} per open conflict whose block is non-empty, appended by the driver right after the briefs are written and before any dispatch — ids parsed back out of the rendered block via `renderedReceiptIds` (already exported from run-engine.mjs) so they cannot drift from what the resolver read.
5. M3 amendment (folded in from run-159 task 7): the `tip unmoved` guard fires only when the prior attempt was not `conflict parked` — a parked attempt reached no candidate, so re-folding the same tip after a park is the first fold of that tip.

Verification: proof leg 1 runs a file I do not own and that is absent at BASE, so I iterate against a throwaway rig under /tmp (bare origin + full clone + integration branch, canned resolver in RESOLVER_SCHEMA's shape, empty testCmd) driving publishFold directly at attempts 1 and 2. Nothing of that rig lands in the tree.

payload.body:
Landed as 3ec6b104, one file: fleet/publish-fold.mjs (+92/-37). Peer's exam path fleet/tests/test_publish_fold.mjs left untouched — absent at BASE and absent here.

What a later session would otherwise have to rediscover, from driving the rig for real:

- The rig works exactly as the Context describes it. publishFold(opts, deps) with deps { makeAgent, exec: execSeam } drives end to end with no boot script: seed a.txt/b.txt, commit = BASE, main moves line 2, the run's branch moves line 2 differently, bare origin + full clone with refs/remotes/origin/HEAD -> main, integration clone at <runDir>/clones/integration checked out at BASE, launch.json { tasks: [] }, args.json {} (no testCmd, so a green fold ends 'folded' with suite 'none').
- The canned resolver's hunk id must be the one the hunks file names on its first line: the file's grammar is 'HUNK h1 lines 2-6' (then '--- context', '--- conflict', '<<<<<<< begin added frontier' / '======= begin added run-<N>' / '>>>>>>> end conflict'). A reply whose id is not that is rejected twice by cmd_resolve ('missing reply for h1') and the attempt ends 'conflict parked' rather than 'folded' — which is a rig bug that reads exactly like an implementation bug.
- Measured on that rig: attempt 1 with a BLOCKED resolver appends resolver:reply label resolve:publish-fold:1:1:1 paths ['a.txt'] evidence.read 'BLOCKED: <notes>', then driver:publish-fold disposition 'conflict parked' paths ['a.txt'] pathsConflicted 1; no driver:facts and no FACTS: in resolver-brief-1-1.txt. Re-driving attempt 1 (the replayed site) appends a second driver:publish-fold with the same paths and pathsConflicted 1. Attempt 2 on the unmoved tip dispatches resolve:publish-fold:2:1:1 (not 'tip unmoved'), its resolver-brief-1-2.txt ends in a FACTS block of exactly two '- receipt' lines in ascending id, the log holds exactly one driver:facts { label: 'resolve:publish-fold:2:1', receipts: [those two ids] }, and with a RESOLVED reply the attempt ends 'folded'. A rig whose two sides edit different files folds with no paths and no evidence key. A rig whose attempt 1 ended 'folded' still ends attempt 2 'tip unmoved' with nothing dispatched.
- The driver:facts rows are appended once per open conflict right after the briefs are written and before any dispatch, not inside the block function: resolveConflicts calls contendingBlock once per resolver ATTEMPT (up to 2 per conflict), so appending from inside it would double-count a rejected reply.
- Green here besides: test_resolver_brief, test_facts_block, test_run_engine_review_economy, test_sims_are_hermetic, test_engine_coverage, test_doctor_rows; git diff --quiet BASE -- fleet/roles/ clean.

payload.author: exam:B@run-160
payload.body:
examiner (run-160 task B), round 1: exam written whole at the guarded path `fleet/tests/test_publish_fold.mjs`. Red at BASE at leg (a)/M1 — `0 !== 1` resolver:reply rows — with every sim precondition green before it (the rig stands, the kernel narrates one conflict on a.txt, the resolver is dispatched at resolve:publish-fold:1:1:1, the attempt parks). Verified green against a scratch implementation of M1-M4 (onEvent wired, both driver:publish-fold sites through publishFoldEvent(row, conflictsIndex()), writeResolverBriefs taking `receipts` and appending factsBlock, the tip-unmoved guard narrowed to a prior attempt that folded, one driver:facts per non-empty brief). Whole file runs in ~1.5 s green / ~0.4 s red — four kernel folds, far under the 300 s cap.

Two readings of legs a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct:

1. leg (c) — the `FACTS:` block's rows are snapshotted BEFORE attempt 2 is driven. `foldReceiptOf`'s own doc says a fold that ended `folded` over conflicts that WERE resolved still leaves a receipt, so attempt 2's own `driver:publish-fold` row is a third receipt on a.txt. Reading the log after attempt 2 returned would render three `- receipt` lines, not the two the leg names. M3's words — 'the rows on the log when the attempt starts' — are what the exam encodes, and it compares the brief's tail byte-for-byte against `factsBlock(<those rows>, ['a.txt'])`.

2. the rigs are separate per scenario for the same reason: leg (b)'s replay of attempt 1 grows the parked rig's log, so leg (c) gets its own parked rig. Order in the file is: parked rig -> (a), (b) clause 1, (d), then its replay -> (b) clause 2; a second parked rig -> (c) clauses 1-4; a clean rig (main edits b.txt, the run edits a.txt) -> (b) clause 3 and (c)'s last clause.

Nothing is unsatisfiable. No action a Proof leg names was substituted: every leg's action is the one the Proof states, driven through `publishFold(opts, deps)` with only the documented `makeAgent` seam canned.

payload.author: impl:A@run-160
payload.body:
Task A landed: driver:finding (blocking + hollow-exam minor), driver:finding-refuted (flaky / exam-concern-upheld / clean), and a receipt on handshake:finding. Three notes a later session would otherwise rediscover:

1. plan-defect (disclosure only): the Context says the rigs for every case already exist in fleet/tests/test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs — the #944 flaky exam and the #908 exam-concern legs. They do not. TOGGLE at line ~1001 is a Run: command for the review-economy probe and has the OPPOSITE polarity (green first, red second), and grepping the file for flaky|rerun|exam:|cannot pass|DONE_WITH_CONCERNS turns up one unrelated line. I built both rigs myself on top of factsRun: FLAKY_EXAM (red once, green on re-run, via a seen.txt marker) for case (i), and an always-red exam plus a fix reply carrying an 'exam: … cannot pass for any output' concern for case (ii). Every leg passes; nothing was unsatisfiable.

2. receiptPathsOf is the one guard that no row carries an empty paths. M1 says a detail naming no path falls back to the whole sorted touch set; I read that same fallback onto M2's and M3's rows, whose natural paths are the exam landings. Declared as an amends: clause.

3. Case (i) uses proofTests.map(landingOf) rather than examLandings on purpose — the pre-review pass runs before the review round declares const examLandings, so the名 would be in its TDZ. Same value, computed early.

Footprint is exactly the three declared FILES. All 38 sims in fleet/tests/ are green.

payload.author: exam:A@run-160
payload.body:
Exam written for run-160 Task A, both guarded sims, red at BASE for the absent implementation only.

proof-runs (legs a–h, k): 13 new runs on `factsRun` (NOT `scenario()` — its fix arm hard-codes `doneImpl` with no `concerns`, and its stub never receives `runDir`, so legs (f) and (d) are impossible on it). Readings a later session would have to reconstruct:
• headSha: a blocked/failed report row carries no `headSha`, so `evidence.against` is pinned against the 40-hex on the engine's own `review:T1:<n>` prompt `HEAD:` line (`aHeadSha`), which is the same `impl.headSha` the capture derived.
• leg (e)'s flaky rig: the existing `TOGGLE` (line 1001) is a *proof-run* command, green-then-red. Leg (e) needs an *exam* red-then-green, so `A_EXAM_TOGGLE` writes a marker in the graded clone; the examiner's `base` probe runs in a different clone and so cannot pre-green the graded pass.
• leg (d)'s hollow rig: the engine only READS `state-exams/`, so the record is written from the impl stub into `<runDir>/state-exams/task-T1/s-0/{walls.json,mutant.json}`, and each of the three variants first asserts `row.stateExams` as a sim precondition.

handshake (legs i, j): two runs of the file's own `driveRun` — run E's rig (an `expected` the captured tree lacks) and run F's (a three-element `content`) — rather than reaching into those blocks, whose bindings are local. The `<headSha>` is read straight off the repository before the run: `withPatchCapture` sets `reply.headSha` to `rev-parse HEAD` in the clone, `patchAgainstBase` never commits and `cloneAtBase` leaves it detached at BASE, so it is the provision-time head for the whole run. Leg (j) is green at BASE by construction (the keys are simply absent there); it is a guard against the implementation attaching a receipt to the shape-refusal case.

Verified rig-soundness rather than assuming it: a throwaway copy of each file with only the new receipt assertions softened runs clean — handshake prints ALL TESTS PASSED, proof-runs prints ALL TESTS PASSED with 28 soft failures, every one of them a missing `driver:finding`/`driver:finding-refuted` row or its fields. No sim precondition fails. One rig defect was caught that way and fixed: `aRunOne` destructured a `row` `factsRun` does not return, so legs (c), (d) and (g) would have died on a TypeError instead of on the clause.
